title: Ultrasound neural maps identify pathology-defined prostate cancer tissue
summary: A three-dimensional CNN and multilayer perceptron combined quantitative ultrasound features to map clinically significant prostate cancer. Development involved 250 patients, followed by 77 later-enrolled patients; reported voxel-level AUC was 0.884 in that later group. Pathology registration and a surgical-enriched cohort limit interpretation. This does not establish patient-level diagnostic accuracy, biopsy benefit or equivalence to MRI-guided care.
ai_technology: Three-dimensional convolutional neural network; multilayer perceptron
organization: Eindhoven University of Technology; Amsterdam UMC; Leiden University Medical Center; Angiogenesis Analytics

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Patient-partitioned development and temporally separate same-centre testing, using reconstructed prostatectomy pathology or negative MRI/biopsy references.
evidence.unknown: Lesion/patient-level clinical performance and treatment benefit remain unestablished; entire-dataset feature standardization and registration uncertainty limit a strictly untouched-test interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Three CNN feature branches learn ultrasound patterns and an MLP combines them into voxel-level cancer probability maps.
